title: Work as the democratic bargain
text: Work gives people competence, independence, social standing and a stake in the future; the democratic bargain rests on the expectation that effort can improve one's circumstances.
use: For 'Rise of Artificial Intelligence: the threat of jobless future...' (2019) and 'There can be no social justice without economic prosperity...' (2020).

title: Teach to fish, not hand out fish
text: On rationalising free food, the authors cite the adage that it is better to teach a person to catch fish than to hand out a free fish every day.
use: For 'A society that has more justice is a society that needs less charity' (2023).

title: The grass that gets trampled
text: A Raipur store manager who went to Russia for a job says he was jailed and pressured to join the Russian army in the war against Ukraine; his family, spending on lawyers, only wants him home.
use: For 'When two elephants fight, it is the grass that gets trampled' (2026).

title: A simple idea with large consequences
text: Tamil Nadu employs 40.3% of India's directly employed women factory workers, helped by dormitories near factories that solve women's two main barriers: distance and a safe place to live.
use: For 'All ideas having large consequences are always simple' (2024) and 'Patriarchy is the least noticed yet the most significant structure of social inequality' (2020).

title: When the architect walks away
text: The US, founder and guarantor of the multilateral order, now rejects it, while a coalition of large and small states from the Global North and South steps in to defend it: the P4M.
use: For 'Has the Non-Alignment Movement (NAM) lost its relevance in a multipolar world' (2017) and 'When two elephants fight, it is the grass that gets trampled' (2026).

title: Hammurabi's eye for an eye
text: In Hammurabi's code, blinding an aristocrat cost you an eye, but blinding a slave cost only a fine: punishment reflected power, not principle. Sabharwal sees the same disease in regulation today: show me the employer, and I'll show you the rule.
use: For 'A society that has more justice is a society that needs less charity' (2023) and 'There can be no social justice without economic prosperity, but economic prosperity without social justice is meaningless' (2020).
